description: Semantic specs for the Specs Viewer/Editor page -- a three-panel layout for viewing, editing, and managing project specifications of all types (page specs, architecture, API, data, dependency, constraint). The left panel shows a hierarchical spec tree grouped by application. The center panel shows spec details with inline editing capabilities. The right panel provides an AI chat for spec review, gap analysis, creation, and workflow building. Users can load bundled specs, discover specs from connected apps via UI Bridge, load/save spec files from disk, toggle edit mode for assertions/groups, and build verification workflows from specs.

groups.name: Page Layout and Header
groups.description: The Specs page uses a three-panel layout: a left sidebar for navigation (spec tree), a center panel for detail viewing/editing, and a right panel for AI chat. The page header shows a shield icon, the page title 'Specs', and a mode badge indicating 'viewer' or 'editor' state. This layout enables efficient spec management without switching between views.

assertions.description: Users see the Specs page heading with a shield icon and the title 'Specs', establishing context that this is the specification management area
Users see a mode badge showing either 'viewer' or 'editor' that reflects the current editing state, helping users understand whether modifications are possible

Users see a three-panel layout with a spec tree sidebar on the left, a detail panel in the center, and an AI chat panel on the right, enabling spec navigation, viewing, and AI interaction simultaneously
Users see the AI Chat panel on the right side of the page, providing access to AI-powered spec review, gap analysis, and creation capabilities

groups.name: Connection Bar and Spec Loading
groups.description: The connection bar sits below the page header and provides controls for loading specs from various sources. Users can load bundled specs, load spec files from disk, discover specs from running apps via UI Bridge, and see connection status. The bar also shows stats (total specs, groups, assertions) and provides buttons for edit mode, saving, and workflow building when a spec is selected.

assertions.description: Users can click a 'Bundled' button to load pre-packaged specification files that ship with the runner, providing a quick starting point for spec exploration
Users can click a 'File' button to open a file dialog and load spec files (.spec.uibridge.json, .architecture.uibridge.json, .api.uibridge.json, etc.) from their local disk
Users see a URL input field (defaulting to http://localhost:3001) and a 'Discover' button to connect to a running application and discover its specs via the UI Bridge SDK
When specs are loaded, users see summary statistics showing total specs, groups, and assertions counts, providing a quick overview of spec coverage
When a spec is selected, users can click a 'Save' button to export the spec to a JSON file on disk with the appropriate extension for its type
When a spec is selected, users can click a 'Build Workflow' button to generate a verification workflow from the spec and navigate to the workflow builder with it loaded
When a page spec is selected, users can toggle edit mode with an 'Edit'/'Done' button, enabling inline modification of assertions and groups

groups.name: Spec Tree Navigation
groups.description: The left sidebar contains a hierarchical tree of all loaded specs. Specs are grouped by application name when specs from multiple apps are loaded. Each tree node shows an icon matching its spec type (shield for page-spec, server for architecture, globe for API, database for data, git-branch for dependency, gauge for constraint), a truncated label, and a count of child items. Page specs expand to show their groups as children. Users can click nodes to select them and view details in the center panel.

assertions.description: When no specs are loaded, users see a message saying 'No specs loaded.' with guidance to load bundled specs or connect to an app, preventing a confusing blank panel

Each spec in the tree shows a type-specific icon (Shield for page-spec, Server for architecture, Globe for API, Database for data, GitBranch for dependency, Gauge for constraint) so users can visually identify spec types at a glance
Page specs with groups can be expanded and collapsed via chevron icons, letting users drill into specific spec groups without cluttering the tree
Each tree node displays a count of its child items (enabled assertions for groups, total items for other spec types), giving users a sense of spec coverage without expanding
Users can click a tree node to select it, which highlights the node and updates the center detail panel to show that spec's or group's details

groups.name: Detail Panel - Page Spec Overview
groups.description: When a page spec is selected, the center panel shows a comprehensive overview including the spec ID, description, metadata (categories, page URL, component, element source), and a list of all groups with their assertion counts. Each group shows its category, name, and enabled assertion count. Users can click on groups to navigate to group detail view. In edit mode, groups can be removed and new groups can be added via an inline form.

assertions.description: Users see the selected spec's ID displayed prominently as a heading in the detail panel, confirming which spec they are viewing
Users see the spec's description text, providing context about what the spec covers and its purpose
Users see the list of unique assertion categories used in the spec (e.g., semantic, element-presence, state-consistency), showing the spec's coverage breadth
Users see a list of all groups in the spec with each group showing its category badge, name, and the count of enabled assertions, providing a complete structural overview
When no spec is selected, users see a centered placeholder message saying 'Select a spec from the sidebar to view details', guiding them to make a selection

groups.name: Detail Panel - Group Detail View
groups.description: When a group is selected in the tree (by expanding a page spec and clicking a child group), the center panel switches to show the group's detail view. This includes the group name, category, description, and a list of all assertions. Each assertion row shows its severity badge, enabled/disabled state (eye icon), description, assertion type badge, category badge, and source badge. The assertion list provides a comprehensive view of all checks within a group.

assertions.description: Users see the selected group's name as a heading in the detail panel, with a category badge showing what type of assertions it contains
Users see all assertions in the group displayed as rows, each showing severity (critical/warning/info), enabled state, description, type, category, and source badges
Each assertion shows an eye icon indicating whether it is enabled (open eye) or disabled (closed eye with strikethrough styling), letting users see which assertions are active

groups.name: Spec Editing - Assertions and Groups
groups.description: When edit mode is active (toggled via the Edit/Done button), users gain inline editing capabilities for page specs. In group detail view, they can toggle assertions on/off by clicking the eye icon, remove assertions with a trash button, and add new assertions via an inline form with description and severity fields. In spec overview, they can remove groups with trash buttons and add new groups via a form with name, category, and description fields. All edits are reflected immediately in the spec state.

assertions.description: In edit mode, users can click the eye icon on any assertion to toggle it between enabled and disabled states, controlling which assertions are active for verification
In edit mode, users can click a trash icon on any assertion to permanently remove it from the group, allowing cleanup of obsolete or duplicate assertions
In edit mode, users see an 'Add assertion' button that reveals an inline form with a description textarea and severity dropdown, allowing creation of new assertions within a group
In edit mode on spec overview, users see an 'Add group' button that reveals a form with name, category, and description fields, allowing creation of new assertion groups
In edit mode on spec overview, users can click a trash icon on any group to remove it from the spec, with the selection automatically adjusting if the removed group was selected
When edit mode is toggled on, the mode badge in the header changes from 'viewer' to 'editor', providing clear visual feedback about the current editing state

groups.name: Detail Panel - Non-Page Spec Types
groups.description: The detail panel supports viewing all six spec types beyond page specs. Architecture specs show tech stack, directory structure, patterns, constraints, and features. API specs show base path, auth type, endpoints with methods and parameters, and data models. Data specs show database type, entities with columns, relations, seeds, and migrations. Dependency specs show modules with artifacts and inter-module links. Constraint specs show performance budgets, bundle budgets, browser targets, responsive breakpoints, accessibility rules, and capacity constraints.

assertions.description: Architecture specs display the tech stack with name/version/purpose for each entry, directory structure, architectural patterns with descriptions, constraints, and feature specs with dependency graphs
API specs display the base path, authentication type, a list of endpoints with HTTP method badges and path, and data models with their schema fields including name, type, and required status
Data specs display the database type, entities with their columns (name, type, nullable, primary key indicators), relations between entities, seed data, and migration records
Dependency specs display modules with their artifacts and inter-module dependency links showing source, target, and link type, enabling visualization of project dependency structure

Constraint specs display performance budgets, bundle size budgets, browser targets with min versions, responsive breakpoints, accessibility level, and capacity constraints, providing a comprehensive view of non-functional requirements

groups.name: AI Chat - Review, Create, and Workflow Building
groups.description: The right panel provides an AI-powered chat interface for spec interaction. It supports two modes: Review (for analyzing selected specs) and Create (for generating new specs from scratch). In review mode, quick-action buttons let users trigger common analyses like gap detection and quality review. In create mode, buttons guide creation of page, architecture, API, and data specs. The chat uses a standalone AI session with spec context prepended to messages. When the AI generates spec JSON in code blocks, an 'Apply as spec' button lets users add the generated spec directly to the tree. A 'Build verification workflow' button generates workflows from page specs.

assertions.description: Users see a 'Review' toggle button that activates quick-action buttons for spec analysis: 'Review spec quality', 'Find gaps', 'Suggest improvements', and 'Generate assertions'
Users see a 'Create' toggle button that shows spec creation templates: 'New Page Spec', 'New Architecture Spec', 'New API Spec', and 'New Data Spec'
In review mode with a spec selected, users see four quick-action buttons that populate the chat input with pre-defined prompts for common spec analysis tasks

Users see a textarea input for typing messages to the AI, with contextual placeholder text ('Ask about this spec...' when spec selected, 'Select a spec first...' when none selected, 'Describe the spec you want to create...' in create mode)
Users see a send button (arrow icon) to submit messages, which converts to a stop button (square icon) when the AI is processing, allowing interruption of long-running responses
AI responses are rendered in message bubbles with a bot icon and purple styling, supporting full markdown rendering for formatted output including code blocks and lists
When the AI generates a valid spec JSON in a code block, users see a green 'Apply as [type] spec' button below the message that adds the generated spec to the tree with a single click
In review mode with a page spec selected, users see a 'Build verification workflow' button that generates a verification workflow from the spec's assertions
Users see a session status indicator (green dot for ready, amber pulse for processing) and a 'New' button to close the current AI session and start fresh

groups.name: File Loading and Saving
groups.description: The Specs page supports loading and saving spec files to/from disk via Tauri file dialogs. Loading supports all six spec file extensions (.spec.uibridge.json, .architecture.uibridge.json, .api.uibridge.json, .data.uibridge.json, .deps.uibridge.json, .constraints.uibridge.json) with automatic kind detection from both filename and content structure. Saving exports the selected spec's config as formatted JSON with the correct extension suggested by default. Loaded file specs appear in the tree with 'File' as their app name.

assertions.description: When loading a spec file, the system automatically detects the spec type from the filename extension, falling back to content-based detection (e.g., presence of 'groups' array indicates page-spec, 'endpoints' indicates API spec)
When saving, the file dialog suggests the correct extension based on spec type (e.g., .spec.uibridge.json for page specs, .architecture.uibridge.json for architecture specs)
After loading a spec file, it is automatically selected in the tree and expanded if it has children, letting users immediately view its contents

groups.name: Spec-to-Workflow Pipeline
groups.description: The Specs page can generate verification workflows from any loaded spec. For page specs, it uses the buildSpecWorkflow function to create structured verification steps from assertions. For non-page specs (architecture, API, data, dependency, constraint), it generates a prompt-based workflow with the full spec JSON embedded as an agentic step. Generated workflows are saved via the unified-workflows API and the user is automatically navigated to the workflow builder with the new workflow loaded.

assertions.description: Building a workflow from a page spec generates structured verification steps from the spec's assertions, creating a targeted verification workflow
Building a workflow from non-page specs (architecture, API, etc.) generates a prompt-based workflow that embeds the full spec JSON as context for AI-driven verification
After successfully saving a generated workflow, the user is automatically navigated to the workflow builder tab with the new workflow loaded for review and execution

groups.name: App Discovery via UI Bridge
groups.description: Users can connect to a running application that has the UI Bridge SDK installed to discover its specs. The connection flow involves entering a URL, clicking Discover, and waiting for the runner backend to discover and cache specs via the UI Bridge. Connection status is shown with icons: disconnected (wifi-off), connecting (spinner), connected (green check with app name), or error (red alert with error message). Discovered specs are merged into the tree alongside bundled and file specs.

assertions.description: Users see a URL input pre-filled with http://localhost:3001 and can modify it to connect to any running app with the UI Bridge SDK installed

The connection bar shows real-time connection status with distinct icons: wifi-off for disconnected, spinner for connecting, green checkmark for connected (showing app name), and red alert for errors (showing error message)
Discovered specs are merged into the tree alongside existing bundled and file specs, with discovered specs replacing previous discovered specs while preserving bundled and file-loaded specs
Users can press Enter in the URL input to trigger discovery without having to click the Discover button, providing a faster interaction pattern
